newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov now sees Cardoso re-election vote Jan13.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov now sees Cardoso re-election vote Jan13.

text.p: A vote on a lower house panel in Brazil's Congress on a proposal to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term will probably take place on January 13, not on January 8 as previously thought, a senior government official said.

The change of date would enable the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) to hold a one-day convention on January 12 to decide its official position on the re-election proposal, said the official, who asked not to be named.
But the delay would not affect the government's target of getting re-election approved in the lower house in January. "In January, we'll get it done," the official said.

The PMDB is one of the largest parties in Congress and is split between supporters and opponents of the re-election amendment, which would give Cardoso the chance of standing in the 1998 presidential elections.
The PMDB is expected to allow its deputies to vote as they wish on the proposal.

The official said the government saw little risk of the amendment being defeated in the panel. Once approved, it could be put to votes on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies on January 15 and 23, he said.
Constitutional amendments require two three-fifths majorities in the Chamber of Deputies and in the Senate.

The government wants re-election approved by the volatile Chamber of Deputies before the end of January when the pro-reform president of the lower house, Dep. Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes, is due to stand down.
